sections.overview:
Ayurveda Ophthalmology – Ayurvedic Science That Deals With Eye And Its Disorders 
 Abstract 
 Ayurveda regards the human eye as one of the supreme sense organs, crucial for intellectual development and perceiving the world’s beauty. The eyes begin developing in the 7th week of pregnancy and continue to mature until adulthood. Healthy eyes are essential for clear vision, balance, coordination, and overall quality of life. Neglecting eye care can lead to problems such as eye strain, dryness, infections, or long-term issues like cataracts, glaucoma, and retinal damage, etc. Since the eyes are closely connected to the nervous system and overall body balance, taking care of them is vital for complete well-being. In this context, we will study Ayurveda Ophthalmology (Shalakya Tantra) to understand natural ways to protect and nourish the eyes. In this study, we will also see how Planet Ayurveda is helping people by providing authentic herbal formulations and guidance that support eye health, and strengthen vision naturally.
sections.introduction:
Ayurveda Ophthalmology comes under Shalakya Tantra Vigyaan, which is one of the eight main branches of Ayurveda. This branch focuses on the eyes, head, ears, nose, throat, and upper neck, using natural remedies and therapies to keep them healthy and strong. Neither Acharya Charaka nor Acharya Sushruta clearly defined the term Shalakya, but commentator Dalhana explained it as: “Shalakayah yath karma kriyate taccha shalakayam,” meaning that Shalaka is a tool frequently used for examination and treatment in this branch, therefore the science is called Shalakya Tantra. The word Tantram refers to a method that protects and maintains the body. Shalaka is described as a tool used for piercing or cutting the Netra Patalas (layers or tunics of the eyeball). Although the term Netra Patala refers to the eye structures, this branch is not limited to eye care alone. According to Shivadasa Sena, Shalakya Tantra also deals with diseases of the Karna (ear), Nasa (nose), and Kantha (throat). 
 The Main Sources For Ancient Indian Eye Medicine 
 The foundational knowledge of Ayurvedic Ophthalmology that is the part of Shalakya Tantra (One of the eight branches of Ayurvedic medicine), is primarily derived from the major Samhitas, though the original text, Nimi Tantra which is not available nowadays. Nimi, also known as Janaka-Videha, is the traditional, yet controversial, originator of Shalakya Tantra, said to have taught it after being cursed and losing his body. The very act of opening and closing eyelids is termed Nimesha, derived from Nimi. He is believed to have lived centuries before other prominent figures.

 Global Prevalence Of Vision Impairment 
 The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that a vast number of people live with some form of vision difficulty: 

 Total Affected: At least 2.2 billion people globally have a near or distance vision impairment. 
 Avoidable Cases: In at least 1 billion of these cases, the vision impairment could have been prevented or has yet to be addressed. 
 Age Factor: The majority of people with vision impairment and blindness are over the age of 50. 
 Economic Impact: The annual global cost of lost productivity due to vision impairment is estimated at over US$ 411 billion. 

 Top Causes of Global Visual Impairment & Blindness: The leading causes of vision loss worldwide are conditions that are often treatable or preventable. 

 Uncorrected Refractive Errors: Like nearsightedness, farsightedness, or astigmatism are the main cause of vision impairment. 
 Cataract: Clouding of the eye’s lens; this remains the single leading cause of blindness globally. 
 Diabetic Retinopathy 
 Glaucoma 
 Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD) 

 Prevalence in India: India carries a substantial portion of the global burden of eye diseases, with millions of people affected by blindness and visual impairment. 

 Blindness: Approximately 4.95 to 6.2 million people in India are blind (around 0.36% of the population). 
 Visual Impairment: Around 55 million individuals have moderate to severe visual impairment. 
 Disparity: Blindness and moderate to severe visual impairment are significantly more prevalent in rural areas compared to urban regions. 

 Leading Causes of Blindness in India: Similar to global trends, the most common causes in India are: 

 Cataract 
 Glaucoma 
 Refractive Errors 
 Diabetic Retinopathy

 Improper Diet/Lifestyle (Midhyaahara Vihara): Excessive intake of specific tastes (ushna, kshara, katu rasa), alcohol, or liquids. 
 Sleep Abnormalities (Swapna Viparyaya): Excessive day sleep (vitiates Kapha) or night waking (vitiates Vata/Pitta). 
 Suppressing Urges (Vegavarodha): Suppressing tears (Bhashpa graha) or vomiting (Chardhir vighatath) causes internal pressure (Udavartha Vyadhi) and strains the eyes.

Exposures: Exposing the head to heat (Shiro Abhitapa) or immediately using cool water after heat (Ushnabhitapthasya jala praveshath).

 Classification Of Eye Diseases In Ayurveda 
 Ayurvedic texts provide a very systematic classification of ocular disorders under Netra Roga. Acharya Sushruta described 76 types of eye diseases, while Vagbhata elaborated further and recognized 96 types of eye disorders. These diseases are classified based on the specific part of the eye involved: 

 Sandhigata Roga : Disorders of the junctional areas of the eye 
 Vartmagata Roga : Diseases of the eyelids 
 Shuklagata Roga : Disorders of the white part of the eye (sclera/conjunctiva) 
 Krishnagata Roga : Diseases of the cornea and iris 
 Drishtigata Roga : Disorders of the lens, retina, and optic nerve affecting vision 

 Preventive Principles Of Eye Care In Ayurveda 
 Ayurveda focuses strongly on preventive care to maintain healthy eyes throughout life. Classical texts recommend: 

 Regular washing of eyes with clean, cool water 
 Avoiding excessive screen time and intense light exposure 
 Protecting eyes from dust, smoke, and pollutants 
 Maintaining proper sleep and mental calmness 
 Regular use of herbal eye tonics and Rasayana herbs 
 Anjana (collyrium) and gentle eye exercises are emphasized for maintaining visual strength 

 Ayurvedic Therapies For Eye Health 
 Ayurveda offers specialized therapies to nourish and heal the eyes naturally: 

 Netra Tarpana: Nourishing therapy using medicated ghee over the eyes 
 Anjana: Application of herbal collyrium to cleanse and strengthen the eyes 
 Aschyotana: Instillation of medicated eye drops 
 Seka: Continuous pouring of medicated liquids over closed eyes 
 Nasya: Nasal administration of medicated oils to strengthen sensory organs
